subject: Post-call: Helios probe — benchmark links, prompt set & compression sensitivity
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.dev>
To: Elena Voss <elena@helios.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.dev, neha.kapoor@redwood.dev
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Helios probe — benchmark links, prompt set & compression sensitivity

Elena — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared view.

TL;DR: Helios is a strong fit for a dedicated inference deployment; main open risks are a tight latency SLO (avg tail <= 150ms for 1k/s traffic) and sensitivity to quantization for the domain-specific summarization prompts.

What we covered
- Primary workload: multi-document clinical summaries (avg 900 tokens generated)
- Required throughput: sustained 600–1,000 reqs/min with 20% peak bursts
- Latency objective: median < 80ms, p95 < 150ms; customer willing to trade some cost for tail latency guarantees
- Data posture: PHI-adjacent (no raw PHI in hosted evals), ops team will request SOC2 evidence and audit logs

Initial model and quantization readouts
- Recommended baseline: Llama-3-Chat-70B (fp16) for fidelity testing; lighter candidate: Llama-3-Chat-13B (AWQ-4/16) for throughput testing
- Suggested compression experiments: AWQ variants first (fast to try), then 4-bit GPTQ for lower mem, and finally FP8 pilot for latency-sensitive paths
- Risk note: earlier Helios benchmarks we saw a ~6–12% ROUGE-style drop when moving from fp16 -> AWQ-4 on domain prompts; need to validate on Helios promptset

Deliverables I can provide this week
1) A shared benchmark pack (small suite + sample harness) and the prompt set we discussed (attached).
2) A suggested experiment matrix (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 x 13B/70B x batching profiles) and expected perf estimates.
3) SOC2 readiness checklist and the audit artifacts you requested.

Next steps (proposed)
- Helios: confirm which dataset we can run on (sanitized subset) and whether we can run hosted benchmarks or you prefer a private package.
- Redwood: we’ll spin up a shortbench run (3 days) covering fp16, AWQ-4, and GPTQ-4 for the 13B and selected 70B variant — we’ll share both token-level latency traces and quality deltas vs baseline.

Attachments: promptset_v2.txt (sample prompts + QoE rubric), helios-benchmarks-v1.csv (example harness output), redwood-quant-playbook.pdf (recommended defaults)

Thanks again — I’ll schedule the shortbench once you confirm the dataset.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Voss <elena@helios.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.dev>
Cc: ops@helios.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:28:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helios probe — benchmark links, prompt set & compression sensitivity

Marcus — thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifications and requests from our side: 

1) Dataset: we can provide a sanitized subset of 200 docs from our production stream (anonymized) — ops will share S3 link if that works. We prefer Redwood to run the hosted shortbench if you can sign an MSA addendum around the sanitized data usage.

2) Tail latency concern: we want guaranteed fallbacks if a quantized variant degrades p95 beyond 20% of fp16. Would Redwood autoswitch to a higher-tier variant automatically, or do we want manual rollback?

3) Quality metric: we use a custom fidelity score (weighted n-gram + entity recall). Can Redwood evaluate the delta and add it to the benchmark CSV?

We reviewed the attachments at a high level — one ask: please include the exact prompt shots used (we need to reproduce locally before the shared run).

If this plan sounds right, I can get the ops S3 link and sign the addendum by EOD Monday.

—Elena
Elena Voss | Head of ML Platform, Helios Analytics
elena@helios.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.dev>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.dev>, Elena Voss <elena@helios.ai>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.dev
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helios probe — benchmark links, prompt set & compression sensitivity

Elena / Marcus — quick technical note from infra/bench squad on the compression tradeoffs and suggested safeguards.

Summary of recommended experiment matrix (short version)
- Models: 13B (L3C-13B), 70B (L3C-70B trimmed variant)
- Modes: fp16 baseline; AWQ-4/8 (per-layer), GPTQ-4 (per-channel), pilot FP8 (if driver supports)
- Batch/profiles: 1, 4, 8 token-stream batching for generation; target KV cache warmup to avoid cold-start p99 hits

Quality vs throughput expectations (rule of thumb)
- AWQ-4: fastest memory wins, expected quality delta vs fp16: 4–9% on our clinical prompts — often concentrated on entity recall (proper names and dosage units).
- GPTQ-4: slightly better quality than AWQ at similar size but higher CPU compile cost; memory lower than AWQ in some kernels.
- FP8: promising latency wins on supported HW for 70B in streaming mode, but tooling maturity is lower — recommend only as a later-stage pilot.

Safeguards we’ll implement for the shortbench run
- Canary bake: run a canary traffic slice (5% of requests) through quantized variant for 12 hours; collect fidelity score and token-level divergence.
- Auto-fallback policy: we can configure a policy that if the custom fidelity score drops >15% or p95 increases >20% relative to fp16 baseline, traffic will route to higher-fidelity variant. We prefer doing the first shortbench with manual review on the first run, then enable auto-fallback on agreement.

Deliverables (technical)
- A Jupyter-ready benchmark pack with the exact promptset_v2.txt (full few-shot contexts) and runner scripts (we’ll add the fidelity scoring hooks you requested).
- A per-model artifact with tokenized traces and a JSON/CSV of per-example deltas (we’ll include the entity-level recall breakdown).

Next internal ask for Redwood
- Neha: can you pre-seed the 13B AWQ/GPTQ builds with the promptset and run a single overnight sweep so we have first-pass numbers Wednesday AM?

—Laura
Laura Bennett | Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.dev
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.dev>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Helios probe — benchmark links, prompt set & compression sensitivity

Elena — thanks. Confirming the plan:
- You: share sanitized S3 link + sign addendum (EOD Mon expected) — ops@helios.ai copied.
- Redwood: run hosted shortbench (fp16, AWQ-4, GPTQ-4) against the sanitized subset; initial overnight sweep (13B) kicked off by Neha Wed AM PT; 70B shortbench contingent on data throughput / warmup timings.
- Safeguards: manual gating on first run; if you opt in we’ll enable auto-fallback policy after one approved run.

I’ll send a calendar invite for a 30-min sync Thursday to review the initial 13B sweep results and decide on 70B/FP8 pilot.

Attachments referenced: promptset_v2.txt (attached) — included again in the Drive link below for reproducibility:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBzBenchmarkSuite

If you want the fidelity hook sooner, Laura has added the scoring script to the pack and will surface a quick README in the Drive.

See you Thursday — Marcus
